BrowseHintAll: Reads all identifiers: {0}, from ECUs: {1}. Takes about {2}.
BrowseHintUnknown: Reads the unknown identifiers: {0}, from ECUs: {1}. Takes about {2}.

BrowseCheckStopped: Stopped. Of the {1} ECUs asked, {0} answered.
ConfidenceUnknown: The car answers, the meaning is not known.
ConfidenceCandidate: The car answers, the formula is an educated guess.
ConfidenceReported: Name or formula from one source, not checked.
ConfidenceConfirmed: Checked on a real car against the dashboard or another known value (the test car, or other sources).
BrowseHelpUnknown: The car answers this identifier, but what the value means is not known yet.
BrowseHelpKnown: What the value means and how it is calculated is known; the Source column says where that comes from.
ReadOnlyNote: This program only reads. It never writes to the car, clears faults or unlocks anything.

CarFileMerged: Car file updated to a newer version ({0} → {1}); your findings carried over ({2}). Previous copy: {3}
NoDemoCar: There is no demo car for {0}.

CatalogHint: ECUs, identifiers, formulas and dashboard values come from this file. Findings on the Discovery tab can be added to it.
ResetCatalogHint: Replaces this car file with the installed version. Use it if the file has got mixed up. ECUs and identifiers added from the Discovery tab are lost.
ResetCatalogConfirm: Replace this car file with the installed version? Your additions are lost.
AdapterNoAnswer: The adapter does not answer. Check the port and try 38400 baud.
SafetyText: Keep the car in READY: long sessions keep it awake and drain the 12 V battery. Unplug the adapter when done.
AutoStartLiveHint: The live view starts by itself as soon as the adapter is connected and the car checked: the laptop can stay in the car untouched.
LiveHint: Live view reads continuously and records to a CSV file.
HistorySimilar: {0} km of drives at this temperature
LifeInPending: shown after a drive or a charge
InUseKmHint: 0 for a new car. A used car’s counters include the previous owner’s use, so your share is worked out from the kilometres driven since.
InUseKmRule: Give the kilometres as a whole number (e.g. 29690 or 29,690).
InUseDateRule: Give a date, e.g. 2024-12-04, not in the future.
InUseHint: The day the car came into your use, e.g. 2024-12-04. The yearly figures count from this day.
LifeYearNoStart: enter the date taken into use below
PriceHint: The full price with transfer and taxes. Empty = no price.
LossHint: More is drawn from the grid than reaches the battery: typically 8–12 % charging at home, 3–5 % at a fast charger.
LifeHint: Put into the battery includes regeneration, so the grid energy and the cost are worked out from the energy taken from the battery plus the charging loss. Per year = kilometres since taken into use × lifetime average consumption, divided by the years since.
ReportHint: Makes a PDF of the battery's current values and the fault codes shown on the Fault codes tab. Read the fault codes first to include them. Saved in the reports folder.
ReportNoteHint: Printed in the PDF report under the car's name (optional)
RepSimulated: simulated car, not a real one
RepBatteryNoAnswer: The battery management did not answer, or the read was cut short, so the battery fault codes cannot be rated. Read the fault codes again with the car in READY.
RepFaultsFromFile: From a saved read: it holds only faults, not whether the battery management answered. Read the fault codes from the car to have them rated.
RepFaultsPartial: The faults found are rated, but the read was cut short or a battery ECU did not answer, so there may be more.
RepFaultsSaved: Saved read {0} ({1}); it may be older than the values above.
ReportFromRecordingHint: Makes a report of a recorded session (live_*.csv): the last reading and the whole drive, cells under load included.
RepSpreadFromRest: Measured at rest at {0} (the latest reading was under load).
RepUnderLoadCold: The battery was cold ({0} °C, below {1} °C): in the cold the cells differ more under load, so the rating is at most Attention. Measure again with the battery warm.
RepUnderLoadComment: The cell whose voltage sags most beyond the others under load while driving, its offset at rest taken off. Points to a higher internal resistance. See Cells under load below.
RepNoDrive: No drive data: the session had no driving and no cell reads under load.
RepSpreadLoadValue: average {0} mV, at most {1} mV; {2} reads, current up to {3} A
RepFewLoadReads: The cells are not ranked: it takes at least {0} cell reads under load (at least {1} A) and {2} at rest. Drive longer and stop now and then to collect both.
RepUnderLoadNone: none stands out (at most +{0} mV / 100 A)
RepUnderLoadNoneComment: No cell sags clearly more than the others under load once its offset at rest is taken off.
RepCellStep: The car gives cell voltages in {0} mV steps, so a smaller spread cannot be seen.
RepCellStepLoad: The car gives cell voltages in {0} mV steps: a cell can be anywhere within a step, so the accuracy limit is half a step, {1} mV.
RepLowAtRest: Lowest at rest: {0}. A low rest voltage tells of a cell holding less charge than the others, for example from higher self-discharge, not of internal resistance.
ReportRecordingOtherCar: The recording {0} is from the folder of the car {1}. Choose that car first, so the report names the right car.
RepReadOnly: data only read from the car
RepSohComment: Health as the battery management reports it. A new pack is about 100 %; the warranty limit is usually about 70 %.
RepSpreadComment: Highest minus lowest cell at rest. Under 30 mV is a well-balanced pack.
RepSpreadNoCurrent: The current is not known, so whether the cells were read at rest is not known: the spread is not rated.
RepSpreadLoaded: Read at {0} A: under load the spread grows, so it is not rated. Read at rest (at most 5 A).
RepTempComment: Warmest minus coldest probe. A large spread can point to a cooling problem.
RepIsolationComment: Insulation between the pack and the body. A low value means leakage.
RepFaultComment: Fault codes of the battery management ECUs (the ones the battery values come from).
RepOtherComment: Codes of other ECUs do not affect the battery rating; they are listed at the end.
RepFaultsNotRead: Fault codes were not read before the report.
RepNoFaults: No active or past fault codes.
RepLimitsNote: The ratings are indicative, not manufacturer limits; the limits and their basis are under Limits of the ratings. The values and cells describe the latest reading; the During the drive section describes the session or recording the report is made from.
RepAuxRestNote: The 12 V battery's rest voltage (read with the car standing and the DC/DC not charging it) roughly tells its charge: full about {0} V, half about {1} V (lead-acid, Battery University BU-903). It is indicative only: reliable after hours of rest, and the car's own loads lower it.
RepCellsLine: {0} cells. Lowest {1} V (no. {2}), highest {3} V (no. {4}), spread {5} mV, average {6} V.
RepBasisFaults: An active fault is on now; a past fault has been, not now. Only the battery ECUs' codes count in the rating.
RepBasisIsolation: UNECE R100: at least {0} Ω/V of the working voltage where the battery's DC side and the motor's AC side are connected (100 Ω/V for separate or doubly insulated buses; the stricter one here). For a {1} V battery that is {2} kΩ. The Good limit of {3} kΩ is the program's own.
RepBasisTemp: Battery thermal management research aims at a spread below 5 °C between cells. The Check limit of 10 °C is the program's own. A large spread can tell of a cooling or temperature probe problem.
RepBasisLoad: The program's own limit; there is no published source. Principle: a cell's internal resistance grows as it ages and shows as a voltage sag under load. The limits rise with the measuring accuracy: {0} mV at base (in test drives the same cells varied by up to about 4 mV from drive to drive), half the car's step with coarse cell readings. When the coldest probe is below {1} °C under load, the rating is at most Attention: in the cold the cells' resistance rises, most in the coldest parts of the pack.
RepBasisSpread: Midtronics (a maker of EV battery testers): a healthy pack's cells are within 10–20 mV, and 50–100 mV is a red flag depending on the manufacturer. The limits sit between the two and in the red-flag range.
RepBasisSohWarranty: The program's own limit. For comparison, the maker's battery warranty: {0}
RepHowAgeF: time of reading − battery management date of manufacture
RepHowWearF: (100 % − SOH) / age in years; and (100 % − SOH) / odometer × 10,000 km. Assumes the new battery was at 100 % and is as old as its battery management.
RepHowDcShareF: DC charged kWh / (AC charged kWh + DC charged kWh)
RepHowPer100F: each load read × 100 A / its current, averaged; the offset at rest taken off
RepHowExtraF: below average under load − below average at rest
RepHowBelowRestF: average of the cells − the cell, averaged over reads at {1} A or less
RepHowBelowLoadF: average of the cells − the cell, averaged over reads at {0} A or more
RepHowEnergyF: power × time, added up; driving (power > 0) and regenerated (power < 0 while moving) apart
RepHowDistanceF: speed × time, added up about every second
RepHowCellSpreadF: highest cell voltage − lowest cell voltage, of one read
RepLoadLimitsNote: This drive's load current was about {0} A. The base limits are {1} and {2} mV / 100 A; at low currents and with coarse cell readings they rise with the measuring accuracy. The limits are the program's own (see Limits of the ratings).
RepSagHealth: Health tells of capacity: a cell can be in full health and still sag more than the others. Worth following whether the difference grows over time.
RepSagScale: A typical cell differs by about {0} mV in this drive (the median of all cells). Differences below {1} mV are within the measuring accuracy.
RepSagPer100: mV / 100 A: the extra under load scaled to 100 amps, so drives at different currents compare.
RepSagExtra: Extra under load: the difference of the two. Only this tells of the cell's internal resistance.
RepSagRest: Below average at rest: the same at rest. This offset comes from charge, not resistance.
RepSagLoad: Below average under load: how far the cell stays below the average of all cells under load.
RepSagHead: How to read the table ({0} cell reads under load, at least {1} A; {2} at rest):
RepLifeNote: The car's own counters over its whole life. Energy put into the battery also includes what braking regenerated. The fast charging share and the energy charged per distance are calculated from the counters and the odometer; the latter also includes heating, standing and possibly charging losses, as it is not known whether the car counts charged energy before or after the charger.
RepLifeNoteShort: The car's own counters over its whole life.
RepGridFromCar: Source: car. Values as they are, colours by the program.
RepUnderLoadCalculated: Source: calculated from the session's cell reads.
RepFaultsFromCar: Source: car. Codes and status bits as they are; the failure type's name under the code from SAE J2012-DA and the bit names from ISO 14229-1; the state (active, stored) by the program.
RepBuyer: A PDF file can be edited. The most reliable result is when the buyer is present at the measurement. Compare the VIN with the lower corner of the windscreen and the registration document.
RepMadeBy: Report made by Esco EV OBD Scanner {0}, {1}.
RepFromCarIntro: Shown as they are, converted to units with the car file's formulas. Their correctness rests on the car's ECUs.
RepFromCarList: Battery: state of charge, SOH, energy left, voltage, current, cell voltages, cell health, temperatures|Safety and 12 V: insulation resistance, the 12 V battery's voltage and temperature|Charging: the charge cable state, the charge and discharge limits (where the car gives them)|Battery management: date of manufacture, software and hardware version|Other: odometer, fault codes, the car's lifetime counters
RepCalculatedIntro: Plain arithmetic on the car's values without assumptions. The formulas are under How the figures are calculated.
RepCalculatedList: From the battery: power, cell spread, temperature spread, the average temperature as the average of the probes (where the car does not give it)|From the drive: the figures of the During the drive section and cells under load; they are the program's measurements, not the car's own trip readings|From the counters: the fast charging share, the energy charged per distance|From the date of manufacture: the age
RepEstimatedIntro: Indicative only. The limits and their basis are under Limits of the ratings.
RepEstimatedList: Ratings: Good, Attention and Check, and the overall verdict|12 V battery: its state (rest voltage or DC/DC charging), judged from its voltage, the speed and the pack current|Wear rate: assumes the new battery was at 100 % and is as old as its battery management
RepVinNotRead: VIN: not read from this car yet
RepVinNotGiven: VIN: not given by the car
RepHowTempAvg: Battery average temperature (when the car does not give it)
VinNotGiven: The car did not give its VIN. It can be written in the Text for the report field.
VinNotKept: VIN {0} was not kept for vehicle {1}: the identity check could not confirm it is the same car, and the vehicle already has VIN {2}.
RepSource: Values read as the car file {0} describes. The file also says which values have been verified on a car.
RepDisclaimer: The program reads what the car reports and cannot guarantee it is correct. Calculations and estimates are indicative. This report is not a manufacturer's or workshop's battery test, nor a guarantee of the battery's condition. The program only reads data: it does not write to the car or clear fault codes. The program is free and provided as is, without warranty.
CurrentNote: The cells are in series, so the same current flows through each.
BatteryWaiting: Start the live view to fill in the cells.
MergeResult: New: {0}, with a new sample: {1}, already in the car file: {2}.
ScanRefused: The ECU does not allow reading identifiers ({0}). Stopped.
ScanSilent: No answer or only errors for {0} queries in a row – car asleep? Press Start to resume: From is set to {1:X4}.
ScanAdapterRefused: The adapter refused this ECU's address. Scan stopped.
BadRange: Give the range in hex, e.g. 0100 and 01FF.
BadEcuRange: Give the range in hex within {0}–7FF, e.g. {0} and 7FF.
DeepHint: Also reads each fault's freeze frame (values at the moment of the fault) and counters, so the read takes longer. The Occurred column shows when and at what mileage, if the car file knows where those are; other values are shown raw.
NotRunHint: Checks that the ECU has not run yet (the insulation test, for example, runs only in certain conditions). They are not faults, so they are hidden by default.
DtcSummary: Active faults: {0}, past (not on now): {1}. Checks not run yet (not faults): {2}.
DtcIncomplete: The read was cut short. So far active faults: {0}, past (not on now): {1}. Read again to get every ECU.
DtcShowingFile: Showing the saved read {0}. It holds faults only; ECUs without faults do not appear.
ShowNotRun: Also show checks not run yet
DtcEarlierHint: Every completed read is saved; pick one in the list and press "Show" to open it again.
DtcBit4: not tested since the last clear
DtcLegend: active (red) = failing now · past, not now (yellow) = the fault was seen before but is not on now. This program does not clear fault codes.
CompareHint: A snap reads {0} identifiers of the car file (known and discovered) from {1} ECUs once and saves them. Takes about {2}. Values that seldom change ({3}) and identifiers the ECU refused to give when scanned ({4}) are read only if you choose them above. Take a snap before and after a change, such as charging, heating or the lights, and compare them: the list shows which values changed and by how much. An identifier that changes only with the change is probably linked to it.
EcuRanges: ECUs answer diagnostics on CAN addresses of their own. The OBD standard's addresses are 7E0–7E7 (replies 7E8–7EF); the maker chooses the others. The car file {2} lists ECUs at {4}; main range {0}–{1}. The wide range searches {3}–7EF, except the addresses ECUs answer on (e.g. 7E8–7EF). Addresses smaller than {3} are not searched: some of them are the car's ordinary messages, and probing them can leave fault codes. Known ECUs at smaller addresses are checked by the "Test the link to the selected ECUs" button on the ECUs tab.
EcuRangesNoMain: ECUs answer diagnostics on CAN addresses of their own. The OBD standard's addresses are 7E0–7E7 (replies 7E8–7EF); the maker chooses the others. The car file {0} lists ECUs at {2}. The wide range searches {1}–7EF, except the addresses ECUs answer on (e.g. 7E8–7EF). Addresses smaller than {1} are not searched: some of them are the car's ordinary messages, and probing them can leave fault codes. Known ECUs at smaller addresses are checked by the "Test the link to the selected ECUs" button on the ECUs tab.
EcuAddNew: Add new ones to the car file
EcuAdded: New ECUs added to the car file: {0}. They now show on the ECUs tab and in the list of step 2.
EcuNotSaved: Saving: the search itself saves nothing; what is found shows in the list and the log. NEW = the car file does not have that ECU. The "Add new ones to the car file" button adds them to {0} as "Unknown ECU 0x…" with their addresses, so their identifiers can be found in step 2.
ScanSaved: Saving: every scan is saved while it runs to a file of its own in this car's scans folder (the "Open folder" button opens it). Findings go into the car file {0} only with the "Add to car file" button, which adds the latest scan made here: new identifiers as unknown, a new sample for ones already found. Older scans can be added with the command line's merge.
EcuHowItWorks: The search only asks each address whether an ECU is there (if no answer comes, it asks once more in another way) and changes nothing in the car.

ErrAdapterRefused: The adapter refused the command {0} that points it at an ECU. Disconnect and connect again; if it repeats, the adapter may not support this.

ErrBleNotFound: The adapter {0} was not found. Check that it is plugged into the car, the car is switched on and the laptop's Bluetooth is on.
ErrBlePairing: Pairing with {0} did not succeed ({1}). Unplug the adapter, plug it back in and connect within 5 minutes: some adapters (e.g. OBDLink CX) accept pairing only for a while after power on.
ErrBleNoService: {0} does not seem to be an ELM327 or STN adapter: it has no service for commands and replies.
ErrBleRefused: {0} did not allow the connection ({1}). Unplug the adapter, plug it back in and connect again.
ErrBleNoAnswer: Bluetooth did not answer in time for {0}. Check that the adapter is on and near, and connect again.
BleAdapterSaved: The adapter used last time (not heard yet)
BleConfigBroken: The Bluetooth LE settings could not be read; the defaults are used: {0}

ErrPortMissing: Port {0} was not found. Plug in the adapter and refresh the port list.
ErrProtocol: The car file's protocol is not supported. Supported: 6 (11-bit CAN, 500 kbit/s) and 8 (250 kbit/s).
CarFileRepaired: Your copy of the car file could not be read, so the original took its place. The broken copy: {0}
CellsUnderLoadHint: How much more each cell sags under load than the others, with its offset at rest taken off, scaled to 100 A. It needs both accelerating and stopping, so there is usually a result after a few minutes of driving. You can also open an earlier recording. A cell that stands out points to a higher internal resistance.
CellLoadWaiting: Fills in while driving. The cells are read about every 15–20 seconds, and more often when accelerating; it takes {1} reads under load (accelerating, at least {2} A) and {4} at rest (stopped, at most {5} A). Usually there is a result after a few minutes of driving. So far: {0} under load, {3} at rest.
CellLoadReady: {0} cell reads under load (about {2} A) and {1} at rest.
CellLoadOpenRecordingHint: Show the cells under load of an earlier live view recording (live_*.csv).
CellLoadTooFew: The recording has too few reads: {0} under load (needs {1}, at least {2} A), {3} at rest (needs {4}, at most {5} A).
ReportNotePlaceholder: e.g. whose car, why it was checked
LegendLoadCold: Colours: green below {0}, yellow at {0} mV / 100 A or more. No red: the battery is cold ({1} °C, below {2} °C), and in the cold the cells differ more under load. Measure again with the battery warm.
LegendLoad: Colours: green below {0}, yellow below {1}, red at {1} mV / 100 A or more (the program's own limits; at low currents the limits rise with the measuring accuracy).
LegendCells: The colours show how the cells differ from each other, not their condition: red is the lowest, green the highest. The colour scale spans at least 20 mV, so a small difference shows only as light shades. Frame: the lowest and highest cell.
LegendHealth: The colours compare the cells' health with each other: red is the weakest, green the best. The colour scale spans at least 2 percentage points, so a small difference shows only as light shades. Frame: the weakest and best cell.
LegendTemps: The colours show how the probes differ from each other: blue is the coldest, red the warmest. The colour scale spans at least 4 °C.
HistoryCollectingNote: the estimate comes after {0} km of drives
RecordingPickHint: This car's recorded live views, newest first. Drives stand out by their kilometres and cell reads under load.
RecordingLine: {0}–{1}  ·  {2} min  ·  {3} km  ·  cell reads under load {4}, at rest {5}
RecordingNone: There are no recordings for this car yet. Start the live view on the Dashboard or Battery tab.
LiveRunningNotice: Live view running: this tab's actions are available once you stop it.
